newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Oil shares tumble in Nigerian stock market.
newsitem.headline: Oil shares tumble in Nigerian stock market.

text.p: Oil shares suffered their worst day at the Nigerian stock market on Thursday as investors dumped the stocks which are usually in hot demand, traders said.
The all-share index fell further to 8605.90 from 8621.43 on Wednesday.
Traders and analysts have attributed the trend to several factors including illiquidity and a misunderstanding of a newly introduced automated clearing system.
Oil shares, previously the toast of the market, fell as dealers came under pressure to sell large volumes, traders said.
Hardest hit were African Petroleum, Agip and Unipetrol, which recorded big losses.
African Petroleum fell by 65 kobo to 57.00 naira, Unipetrol was 69.00 naira, down 58 kobo and Agip finished 60 kobo lower at 21.40 naira.
Only Texaco rose 10 kobo to 49.50 naira buoyed by rising demand in anticipation of improved profits.
The slump also continued in the banking sector but fewer shares in the sector were affected on Thursday.

Only Union Bank, 20 kobo down at 13.70 naira, and UBA, five kobo down at 12.10 naira closed weaker while FSB international Bank, at 4.20 naira and Guaranty Trust Bank at 13.30 naira were five kobo and 10 kobo stronger, respectively.
Nigerian Breweries and Guinness shed 10 kobo apiece to 19.90 naira and 7.70 naira, respectively.
